title: Security Audits
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 6: Security Assessment and Testing: Security Audits.

items: Internal audit — Conducted by organization's own audit team
External audit — Conducted by independent third-party auditor
Compliance audit — Verifies adherence to specific regulations (HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX)
Operational audit — Evaluates efficiency and effectiveness of operations
Financial audit — Examines financial statements and controls
SOC 1 — Financial reporting controls (relevant to financial audits)
SOC 2 — Security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, privacy (Trust Services Criteria)
SOC 3 — Same as SOC 2 but public-facing summary (no detailed findings)
Type I — Controls at a point in time (design adequacy)
Type II — Controls over a period of time (operational effectiveness, typically 6-12 months)

rows: Control design at a point in time
Control design at a point in time — "Do appropriate controls exist?"
Control effectiveness over 6-12 months — "Do controls actually WORK over time?"
Same scope as SOC 2 but no detailed findings

blocks.text: Trust Services Criteria (TSC) — SOC 2 evaluates these 5 categories:

items: Security (required) — Protection against unauthorized access
Availability — System is available for operation and use
Processing Integrity — Processing is complete, accurate, timely
Confidentiality — Information designated as confidential is protected
Privacy — Personal information is collected, used, retained, and disposed of properly

blocks.text: Type I vs Type II — The Critical Distinction:

rows: Lower — controls may exist on paper but not in practice
Higher — proves controls operated effectively over time

blocks.text: From Destination CISSP: "Companies have this evaluation done so they can use this as a selling point to attract new customers and provide confidence for their current customers." Manager Decision: Which SOC Report to Request?

items: Evaluating a cloud provider's financial controls → SOC 1
Evaluating a SaaS provider's security → SOC 2 Type II (strongest assurance)
Quick initial assessment of a new vendor → SOC 2 Type I (sufficient for initial evaluation)
Marketing to general public → SOC 3 (shareable without NDA)
Due diligence before contract → SOC 2 Type II (proves controls work over time)

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: SOC 2 Type II is the GOLD STANDARD because it evaluates controls over a period (usually 6-12 months), proving they actually work over time. Type I only proves they were DESIGNED properly at a single point. ⚠️ Exam Trap: SOC 2 reports contain sensitive details and are shared under NDA. SOC 3 reports are the public-facing version with no sensitive detail. If the question says "share with the general public" → SOC 3. ⚠️ Exam Trap: SOC 1 is about FINANCIAL controls (relevant to financial audits). SOC 2 is about SECURITY controls. Don't confuse them — if the question mentions financial reporting, it's SOC 1. If it mentions security, availability, or privacy, it's SOC 2.

items: SSAE 18 — Statement on Standards for Attestation Engagements (U.S. — AICPA)
ISAE 3402 — International Standard on Assurance Engagements (international)
Frameworks for service organization audits
Replace the older SAS 70 standard
Govern how SOC reports are created and structured
Statistical sampling — Uses mathematical methods for representative sample
Non-statistical (judgmental) sampling — Based on auditor's judgment
Sample must be random and representative of the population
Results from sample are extrapolated to the entire population
Larger samples provide greater confidence but cost more

blocks.text: From Chapple: "Sampling only works if it is random! Don't allow system administrators to generate the sample or select the items to include in the sample." If sampling reveals no significant flaws, "they make the assumption that this is representative of the entire population." However, the auditor must document:

items: How the sample was selected
Sample size justification
Confidence level achieved
Any anomalies found in the sample

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: The AUDITOR must control the sampling process. If the auditee selects which items are examined, the results are meaningless because they could cherry-pick favorable examples.
